+## #3179 - Export one selected die opening for inspection
+
+The operator can create a nominal inspection operation on the Classic 2S template with an empty machining condition. It stores the selected chain and the operator’s start point. It survives undo, redo and project reload. Ordinary generation still requires a valid resident condition.
+
+The operator can export the nominal contour of one saved Wire Contour to a new Classic 2S inspection piece. The ISO preserves the LINE and ARC spans of the selected DXF chain in the setup work frame. Its SBL imports one work, a 3 mm threading hole and zero working steps. The receipt identifies the chain and the number of nominal spans.
+
+The inspection piece uses zero native length and width for unknown physical stock XY. An offline control saved and reopened those values. The project box supports drawing placement and the 10 mm height. It supplies no claim about the physical stock footprint.
+
+The inspection piece requests the reference settings for 10 mm steel 0001 and Berco Cut 0.25. An offline control displayed the QREF10 reference quality and zero steps. The effective erosion offsets, installed travel, workholding and entry and exit paths still need separate verification. The existing machining post retains its verification requirements. The export does not use a generated wire centreline or infer a slug catcher.
+
+The inspection action checks the entire threading disk and the nominal contour against the other drawing primitives. A retraced line on the same layer belongs to the selection only when the chainer identifies its original and both endpoints match exactly. The export rounds ISO coordinates to five decimals and checks the resulting contour again. A synthetic R2 corner with a 0.000005038 mm difference between the rounded endpoint radii registered as a closed CCW die contour in the offline control. Larger discrepancies are refused. All three files become visible together in a new directory.
+
+The mounted machine's X and Y limits apply in the selected work frame. The export checks analytic arc extrema before and after coordinate rounding. The native format used here cannot carry reversed axis polarity. An unspecified travel limit stays unverified. The controller displays a perpendicular lead default and the nominal Z datum. Neither establishes the physical stock position or a verified lead trajectory.
+
+Machining this geometry would require verified leads, effective resident technology and physical slug retention. Those inputs belong in the cutting workflow.

+## #3180 - Use one selected DXF chain for a Wire Contour
+
+**Decision.** The operation stores the existing sketch entity and stable chain ID. The resolver keeps the ordered analytic segments, their original primitive indices and the stock-face placement. Generic generation accepts a closed chain of straight segments with coincident joints. The existing wire generator applies the machine condition's signed kerf offset once. The post checks the nominal profile through the full height of the box stock.
+
+**Reason.** The chain supplies the finished outline. The operator specifies the punch or die side, threading point and physical slug capture. A through cut needs stock at every height. Every unselected primitive, including rejected chain fragments, must clear the full bounding box of the cut, its lead, kerf and released piece. A primitive on a separate layer has the same protection.
+
+**Alternatives dropped.** Reading the entire drawing can cut an unrelated chain. Chords change an analytic arc and move its offset. A stock silhouette cannot verify a sketch's nominal outline. An earlier operation can change the material that holds the piece. This first case uses fresh axis-aligned box stock, one placed drawing and a single vertical pass. The resolver refuses additional bodies and unverified boundary controls.
+
+**Cost to change.** An analytic consumer can use the same selected chain and placement. It must bound its actual leads and kerf, verify its signed offset and prove slug retention. Additional stock shapes, sequential cuts, fixtures and tabs need corresponding material and clearance checks. The project format already stores the stable pick.
+
+The drawing computes its exact primitive signature at construction. An operation status read uses that stored value. Reopening a project reconstructs the signature from its primitives. A coordinate edit below the chain ID quantum changes the signature.

+### Agie nominal inspection
+
+Mount the Classic 2S template on the active setup. Place a DXF on the top of a 10 mm reference box and set the work Z origin at its top. Use `list_features` to identify the closed chain. Pass its ID, drawing name, operation name, 0.25 mm wire tool and the centre of the 3 mm hole to `create_agie_inspection`. The start coordinates are world XY in millimetres. The operation has no machining condition and can be saved and reopened.
+
+Call `export_agie_inspection` with the saved operation name and a new directory. The last part of the directory name supplies the uppercase DOS file stem. The CLI equivalent is `camcraft-cli export-agie-inspection <project.camproj> <operation> <new-directory>`. The desktop creation form is under **Setup → Post → Agie nominal inspection**. Select the saved operation to use **Export Agie inspection setup**.
+
+Import the ISO geometry and keep its SBR beside the SBL during script import. Create a new piece and confirm zero working steps. The native piece has zero length and width because physical stock XY is unknown. The contour uses the project work datum. Physical stock Z and travel without stated machine limits remain unverified. The work selects the controller’s perpendicular lead default. Holding, actual entry and exit paths, and effective erosion settings remain unverified.
+
+On the offline Classic 2S, the formal check of the work reports undefined technology (`Technologie: te definiëren`). Checking the whole piece also reports that its dimensions are too small (`Dimensions X, Y, Z: Waarde te laag`), because the inspection piece records zero for its unknown length and width.
